fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Healthy Men as Natural Leaders", "body": "Dylan argued that healthy, confident people should show themselves in the truth community instead of giving up and resenting everyone. He said men who stopped chasing women and pursued a craft or a mastery would eventually make a dent in the world. Chance said that as his own health improved, family members listened to him more, and he called that natural leadership. He also described both extreme obesity and an extreme hard body as forms of armoring around the biofield, with strong but flexible in the middle."}, {"title": "Taking Responsibility for Your Own Programming", "body": "Dylan used the film Vanilla Sky to explain how he came to see his own difficult stretch as a nightmare he had programmed through his choices and beliefs. He argued that people were sold a prescribed path to success and that taking responsibility, rather than blaming others, was the way out. He said he was writing two books, one covering the mistakes he made and the routine he used to turn things around. Chance agreed that the outer shell reflected the inner self."}, {"title": "Rejection, Polarity, and the White Knight Habit", "body": "Dylan argued that his years as an actor taught him to be comfortable with rejection, and he suggested improv classes for anyone afraid of embarrassment. Chance said being too much of a white knight had been one of his own downfalls, and he compared healthy relationships to the poles of a battery that needed distinct polarity. Dylan argued that constantly conceding to a partner could make a person less attractive, and he described alpha and beta as directions of behavior rather than fixed types."}, {"title": "Trade Skills, Time, and Language Study", "body": "Chance relayed chat comments that trade skills were attractive and valuable, and Dylan argued that a needed profession gave a person leverage against a dystopian system. Dylan said time was the one thing nobody got back and argued that his Spirit Whirled books could help readers catch up without wasting years. Chance said he stayed interested in etymology and philology and argued that studying language explained why people thought what they thought. He also recommended a dense author whose books chart wordplay across languages."}, {"title": "Call-Ins, Visitors, and Closing Plugs", "body": "Allen Marcus left a voicemail quoting Mark Passio on righteous anger and describing a viral beach confrontation he found embarrassing. Carol Hall arrived in person with gifts for Chance, then joined the call and said her biggest flat earth proof point was how the globe model diminished human value. Gordan Hamil called in to describe overhauling his diet and lifestyle, and the show closed with a plug for a Friday Telegram event called Mystic Knights of the Midnight Movie. Dylan closed by plugging his Spirit Whirled series and asking readers to leave reviews."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Vibe Rant returns to your brainwaves, joined by Dylan Saccoccio, author of the Spirit Whirled series.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "You might not make a lot of money at it after 10 years, but eventually you'll start making a dent and having an impact on people. And if you focus on making an impact rather than making money, people notice that. And the biggest thing I think anybody can do is focus on trying to achieve their best version of themselves.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "You can't be all wrong, right? It's not just about health. The more you can succeed at your life, the more others are going to be apt to listen to you. And that's what natural leadership is really about.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Obesity is a type of armoring that we do around our field. It's a bio energetic thing, but so is the extreme hard body type where their biceps are big, they can't even touch their shoulder or even close, you know? Both of those can be a bad sign, right? But right in the middle where you're strong, but flexible, where it counts.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's a nightmare, but it's not a nightmare because the world's a nightmare. It's a nightmare because I programmed it to be that way with my own behavior and my own choices. And yes, things happen that are out of our control, but we still have a choice in how we respond when those things happen. Always have a choice in every moment.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Once you can get comfortable with being embarrassed, comfortable with rejection and not taking anything personally, you can really thrive in environments where other people are too scared to take chances because they're in their own heads, thinking too much about what other people think of them, not realizing that most people don't think of you at all.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "That's one of the hard things to come to terms with, someone like me who spent the majority of my adult life figuring out what's going on in this world, from Hollywood to banking, and I had to figure everything out the hard way. I spent all that time looking into that stuff that I neglected the things that make a man a man.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "That's part of what makes the spark fall out, is that we are like poles in an electrical system or battery and you need the polarity to be distinct. You need the North and the South, or there's not going to be a spark in the gap, right? If they're both a little bit of both, it's just going to be like this weird neutral thing.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's not about rejecting the opposite sex. It's just about not making that pursuit of a relationship your top priority anymore. This goes for anybody, regardless of gender, honestly. But for men, I think it just is more biologically imperative that we start to wither on the vine and die as soon as we put anything else above our life's purpose, whatever that is.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "No doubt diminishing returns, but learning about language helps you understand why you think what you think. And that's really, really important.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Get as offended as you want, says Mark Passio.
